UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile on NPB Media, storing non-sensitive information for both local and external (e.g., Google) authenticated users. Passwords and sensitive authentication credentials are managed by an external system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, typically provided by an external authentication system.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication and identification.

profilePictureUrl.description: URL to the user's profile picture, if available (e.g., from social login).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Represents a service offered by NPB Media, detailing its features and benefits for display on the website's interactive services showcase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

title.description: The name or title of the service.

shortDescription.description: A concise, AI-assisted summary of the service, used for initial presentation.

longDescription.description: A detailed description of the service, highlighting its features and value proposition.

iconUrl.description: URL to an icon representing the service, for visual identification.

imageUrl.description: URL to a primary image associated with the service, for visual engagement.

displayOrder.description: A numerical value indicating the order in which services should be displayed on the website.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the service record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the service record was last updated.

CaseStudy.title: CaseStudy
CaseStudy.description: Represents a detailed case study or portfolio project by NPB Media, showcasing successful work and client solutions within the dynamic portfolio area.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CaseStudy entity.

title.description: The title of the case study or project.

clientName.description: The name of the client for whom the project was undertaken.

industry.description: The industry sector of the client or project.

briefSummary.description: A concise, AI-assisted summary of the case study's key aspects and outcomes.

fullDescription.description: The comprehensive narrative of the project, including challenges, solutions, and measurable results.

projectUrl.description: URL to the live project or a relevant external link, if applicable.

thumbnailUrl.description: URL to the thumbnail image for displaying the case study in listings and previews.

galleryImageUrls.description: An array of URLs for images showcasing various aspects of the project work.

tags.description: An array of keywords or tags to categorize and filter case studies.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the case study record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the case study record was last updated.

ContactSubmission.title: ContactSubmission
ContactSubmission.description: Stores information submitted through the website's streamlined contact form, enabling efficient lead capture and visitor inquiry management.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ContactSubmission entity.

name.description: The full name of the person submitting the inquiry.

email.description: The email address of the submitter for follow-up communication.

company.description: The name of the company the submitter represents (optional).

subject.description: The subject line or brief topic of the inquiry.

message.description: The full message content from the submitter.

submissionTime.description: Timestamp indicating when the contact form was submitted.

isRead.description: A flag indicating whether the submission has been reviewed by an internal team member.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for NPB Media prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable access by strictly adhering to the core design principles. This involves a clear segregation of data based on its security posture (public, user-private, admin-private) and a consistent application of access modeling patterns.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**

1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** Authorization independence is achieved through path-based ownership. A user's profile document `users/{userId}` is directly tied to their `request.auth.uid`. Security rules can simply compare `request.auth.uid` to `{userId}` in the path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to other documents to determine ownership. This allows for atomic user profile operations.

2.  **Public Content (`/services/{serviceId}`, `/caseStudies/{caseStudyId}`):** These collections are designed for public read access. Since all documents are globally readable, there's no inherent authorization dependency between documents, thus no `get()` calls are required for reading. Administrative write access to these public documents (for content management) is granted by checking the existence of the user's ID in the dedicated `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection. This check is an atomic `exists()` operation, ensuring authorization independence for content modification.

3.  **Contact Submissions (`/contactSubmissions/{submissionId}`):** Anonymous users can create these, but only administrators can read or update them. Authorization for administrators to read/update is determined by their presence in the `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection, using an atomic `exists()` check. No `get()` calls on other `ContactSubmission` documents or parent documents are needed for authorization.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

1.  **Public Content (`/services`, `/caseStudies`):** Both collections explicitly grant public read access. This means `list` operations for these collections will return all documents, as intended, without requiring any client-side filtering or complex server-side rule evaluations that filter results. The security rules fully define the permissible data for `list` operations.

2.  **User Profiles (`/users`):** `list` operations on the root `/users` collection are generally not permitted for security and privacy reasons, preventing users from seeing a directory of all other users' profiles. Access is restricted to `get` operations on individual, owned profiles, or specific, public sub-collections if they were to exist.

3.  **Contact Submissions (`/contactSubmissions`):** `list` operations are secured by restricting them to only authenticated administrators. The security rule will verify the user's admin role using `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` before allowing any `list` operation. This ensures that only authorized users can list the submissions, maintaining the QAP principle.

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**

*   **User-Owned Private Data:** `users/{userId}` uses path-based ownership, a highly secure and simple pattern for individual user data.
*   **Public Read-Only Data:** `services/{serviceId}` and `caseStudies/{caseStudyId}` hold data intended for everyone. Their security posture is globally readable, simplifying rules.
*   **Admin-Managed Data:** `contactSubmissions/{submissionId}` is writeable by anyone, but readable only by admins, demonstrating a specific internal management need.
*   **Global Roles (DBAC):** `/roles_admin/{userId}` standardizes administrator access control via a simple document existence check, avoiding custom claims and centralizing role management.

This structure minimizes complexity in security rules, enhances debuggability, and provides a solid foundation for secure and performant data access.
